install_point: after all Stage-A initialization, immediately before workload exec (never before no_new_privs)
change_control: docs/seccomp-derivation/policy.md section 5: NO UNDOCUMENTED SYSCALL EXPANSION. Any change requires an explicit diff, a documented reason, a security-impact assessment, relevant test changes, and a docs/ADR update. check_trace_regression.py fails any observed syscall outside this list.

changelog.reason: Native Phase C verification on Ubuntu 24.04 / kernel 6.8 / x86_64: git 2.43.0 (ADR-005 toolchain) requires chdir for the closed-set operations (status/diff/ls-files/merge-base/rev-parse) - the -C worktree handling and work-tree-top resolution. Host-side strace of the exact closed set shows 31 distinct syscalls of which chdir is the ONLY one missing from the allowlist (no fork/clone needed; helpers neutralized). Without it git fails inside the sandbox with 'fatal: cannot change to ...: Operation not permitted' (EPERM from the default-deny filter).
changelog.security_impact: chdir is a cwd-only syscall (same class as the already-allowed getcwd): no privilege gain, no namespace/network/filesystem-boundary escape. The path-set enforcement remains the rootfs/pivot_root boundary (division of labor, policy.md section 4); chdir cannot leave the rootfs.
changelog.evidence: tools/seccomp-derivation/trace-results.json t1_git_closedset (native VM trace, 2026-08-22); tests/adversarial/test_git_attacks.py SandboxGitContainmentTests 4/4 PASS on the native substrate; tests/native/test_hardened_e2e.py re-run green.

limitations: Docker/container-validated evidence so far; native ubuntu CI re-run authoritative. Threads (clone) and networking syscalls denied by design. glibc/x86_64-specific. Rootless uid-mapped execution NOT yet validated (Phase 1).
